subject.title: Feature: Telegram Reactions - Two-Way Support with Prompt Guidance

question: Should incoming Telegram reaction interpretation reuse the existing `reactionLevel` and `reactionNotifications` controls, or should OpenClaw add an independent `reactionGuidance` configuration surface?
rationale: Both controls already affect reaction-related model behavior, and adding a third setting changes the public configuration contract and could create conflicting modes; source inspection cannot determine the intended product semantics.

options.title: Consolidate existing controls
options.body: Keep `reactionLevel` as the outbound guidance control and gate incoming soft-signal guidance with `reactionNotifications`, avoiding another public setting.

options.title: Add independent guidance mode
options.body: Add `reactionGuidance: off|minimal|full` with explicit precedence, migration, schema, metadata, documentation, and fresh-install/upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep passive events only
options.body: Retain current reaction events and outbound guidance without teaching the agent a fixed incoming emoji interpretation map.

recommendation.title: Consolidate existing controls
recommendation.body: Keep `reactionLevel` as the outbound guidance control and gate incoming soft-signal guidance with `reactionNotifications`, avoiding another public setting.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the most recent product-level triage on the precise configuration and prompt-semantics question.
